title: Uludağ Ski & Bursa Thermal Weekend From Istanbul
seoTitle: Uludağ Ski & Bursa Thermal Weekend From Istanbul
metaDescription: Plan an Uludağ ski and Bursa Çekirge thermal weekend from Istanbul with 2026 Teleferik fares, snow months, and Zone 1 vs Zone 2 advice.
quickAnswer: A weekend pairing Uludağ skiing with Bursa's Çekirge thermal baths takes roughly two to three hours from Istanbul via ferry or the Osmangazi Bridge. Ride the Bursa Teleferik up to the Hotels Zone for snow between January and March, then soak in historic Ottoman mineral pools down in Çekirge.

body.text: Istanbul residents treat Uludağ as their winter backyard, which means Friday-night traffic and crowded Saturday lifts if you time it poorly. When you pair a morning on the mountain with an overnight down in Bursa's thermal foothills—see our [Bursa destination guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/destinations/bursa) and [Türkiye in winter guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/turkey-in-winter-premium-travel-guide)—you get pine-lined skiing and hot mineral recovery without paying peak mountain hotel surcharges.
How do you reach Uludağ by cable car from Bursa?

Board the [Bursa Teleferik](https://bursateleferik.com.tr/fiyat-tarifemiz.php) at Teferrüç Station in eastern Bursa for a scenic ride via Kadıyayla and Sarıalan straight to Oteller Bölgesi (Hotels Zone). Per [November 2026 local transport tariffs](https://bursatatil.com/uludaga-ulasim-fiyatlari/), an adult round-trip costs 500 TL (250 TL for students), with cabins typically running 10:00 to 18:00 weather permitting.

From Istanbul, reach Bursa either by taking the BUDO or IDO ferry across the Sea of Marmara to Mudanya or Güzelyalı (followed by a 35-minute taxi to Teferrüç) or driving over the Osmangazi Bridge in about two hours. Driving up the 36-kilometer mountain road yourself is an alternative, but Uludağ National Park charges a 225 TL car entry fee via HGS/plate detection, and police enforce mandatory winter tires and snow chains. If high winds pause the cable car, minibuses from Tophane run up to the hotels for 310 TL one way.

items: Teferrüç Station access: Reached in 15–20 minutes by taxi from central Bursa or Çekirge; on-site parking is available.
Wind-hold backup: Always check live operating status at [bursateleferik.com.tr](https://www.bursateleferik.com.tr/) before leaving your hotel, as strong southern lodos winds halt service.
Ski gear on cabins: Standard eight-person cabins carry luggage and skis, though bulky bags are easier to store at your Çekirge hotel while renting gear on the mountain.

body.text: Which months have reliable snow in Uludağ?

Reliable snow in Uludağ runs from late December through mid-March, with January and February delivering the deepest cover and steadiest lift operations. According to [Go Türkiye's Uludağ resort profile](https://goturkiye.com/skiing/uludag) and [30-year snow history](https://www.snowsure.ai/resorts/uludag/guide), the 1,750–2,543 meter ski area averages 49 cm of snowfall in January and 44 cm in February.

For the 2026–2027 winter season, the official [Uludağinfo resort portal](https://www.uludaginfo.com/en) targets an opening around December 18 through March 31. Still, December snow can be thin on lower runs, while late March often turns slushy by early afternoon. Avoid Turkish school mid-term break (late January) and national holiday weekends unless you enjoy 30-minute lift queues. Midweek January and February dates give you fresh grooming, lower hotel rates, and open slopes—if you want higher-altitude dry powder, compare [Erciyes Ski Resort](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/erciyes-ski-resort-cappadocia).
How do you pair skiing with Çekirge thermal baths?

Base yourself in Bursa's hillside Çekirge district, ski Uludağ from 09:30 to 15:00 via the cable car or private driver, then descend for a 17:00 mineral soak and dinner. Historic bathhouses like [Eski Kaplıca](https://visitbursa.org/tr/mekanlar/eski-kaplica-400) and [Yeni Kaplıca](https://yenikaplica.com.tr/) pipe naturally heated geothermal water directly beneath Ottoman stone domes.

Eski Kaplıca (also known as Armutlu Hamam), commissioned by Sultan Murad I over Byzantine foundations and part of Bursa's 2014 UNESCO World Heritage listing, offers atmospheric domed marble pools fed by mineral springs. Yeni Kaplıca runs separate men's and women's sections plus private family rooms (aile banyoları) with traditional kese scrub and massage services. After soaking, eat İskender kebap and candied chestnuts (kestane şekeri) in central Bursa before sleeping in a thermal hotel rather than an overpriced, noisy ski lodge.
What is the difference between 1st and 2nd Development Zones?

Uludağ's two hotel clusters sit roughly one kilometer apart with distinct atmospheres, as detailed in [local Uludağ slope guides](https://agirlinistanbul.com/uludag-ski-resort-bursa-turkey/). The 1st Development Zone (1. Gelişim Bölgesi) is older, denser, and livelier with beginner runs and rental shops; the 2nd Development Zone (2. Gelişim Bölgesi) is newer, quieter, and hosts larger hotels plus the Teleferik arrival station.

body.text: One critical Uludağ quirk: lift networks have historically been split across different operators, so confirm whether your hotel's nearest lift is included in the unified skipass before booking. If you are coming up just for the day by Teleferik, arriving directly in Zone 2 lets you step onto less crowded slopes within minutes.

faq.q: How long does it take to get from Istanbul to Uludağ?
faq.a: Expect 2.5 to 3.5 hours door to door depending on traffic and route. Driving via the Osmangazi Bridge takes roughly 2 hours to Bursa plus 45 minutes up the mountain; ferries to Mudanya take 1 hour 45 minutes before road transfer.

faq.q: Can I do Uludağ as a day trip from Istanbul?
faq.a: Yes, but it is a long 14-hour day. Staying one or two nights in Bursa's Çekirge thermal district turns the trip into a relaxed weekend and gives you flexibility if wind delays the Teleferik.

faq.q: Do I need snow chains to drive up to Uludağ?
faq.a: Yes. In winter, gendarmerie checkpoints on the mountain road require winter tires and carried snow chains on private vehicles. If you prefer not to drive in mountain snow, park at Teferrüç and take the Teleferik.

faq.q: Are Çekirge thermal baths mixed-gender or separated?
faq.a: Traditional historic hammams such as Yeni Kaplıca operate strictly separate men's and women's thermal halls, while also offering bookable private family suites. Modern Çekirge thermal hotels usually have both mixed indoor pools and gender-separated spa areas.

faq.q: Can beginners rent all ski equipment in Uludağ?
faq.a: Yes. Both Zone 1 and Zone 2 have numerous rental shops supplying skis, snowboards, boots, helmets, and waterproof outerwear, plus certified instructors for private hourly lessons.

faq.q: What happens if wind closes the Bursa Teleferik while I am on the mountain?
faq.a: If high winds halt the cable car in the afternoon, minibuses and taxis operate continuously down the main road to Bursa city center for a set per-person fare.
